print([x["id"] for x in items if x["owner"]=="a"])
vector-databases.usage: Restrict retrieval to passages the learner may access.

examples.title: Apply an access filter
examples.code:
items = [{"id":"p1","owner":"a"},{"id":"p2","owner":"b"}]
print([x["id"] for x in items if x["owner"]=="a"])

mistakes: Reusing a vector after its source passage changes can return stale results.
edges: Approximate nearest-neighbor search can miss a true nearest result.
useCases: Passage index
Restrict retrieval to passages the learner may access.
practices: Evaluate filtered retrieval against a small exact-search reference.
vector-databases.interview: What is recall at k for an approximate index? It measures how many desired reference neighbors appear in the returned top k.
vector-databases.miniProject: Design a passage record with an ID, permissions, source version and vector.
exercises: Design a passage record with an ID, permissions, source version and vector.
Describe how a deleted source document is removed from retrieval.

semantic-search.definition: Semantic search retrieves items by similarity of meaning represented in a learned space.
semantic-search.why: Find a discussion of paid time off when the user searches for vacation policy.
semantic-search.explanation: Encode query and passages with a compatible retrieval model. Rank candidates with the expected metric and inspect the highest matches. Evaluate using queries with known relevant passages.
semantic-search.usage: Find a discussion of paid time off when the user searches for vacation policy.
mistakes: A high similarity score does not establish that a passage actually answers the question.
edges: Exact identifiers and uncommon names may be better served by lexical matching.
useCases: Passage search
Find a discussion of paid time off when the user searches for vacation policy.
practices: Evaluate both paraphrases and exact identifier searches.
semantic-search.interview: How can retrieval be evaluated without generation? Compare ranked passage IDs against relevance judgments.
semantic-search.miniProject: Rank passages and calculate recall at two cutoff values.
exercises: Rank passages and calculate recall at two cutoff values.
Create a question that requires an exact product code match.

rag.definition: Retrieval-augmented generation supplies relevant external passages to a model during answer generation.
rag.why: Build an assistant that can answer questions about a local handbook.
rag.explanation: Retrieve candidates, assemble a bounded context, ask for an evidence-linked answer and verify its references. Separate retrieval failures from failures to use retrieved evidence.
rag.syntax:
passages = [("p1","The lab opens at nine."),("p2","It closes at five.")]
print("\n".join(f"[{i}] {t}" for i,t in passages))
rag.usage: Build an assistant that can answer questions about a local handbook.

examples.title: Build a context block
examples.code:
passages = [("p1","The lab opens at nine."),("p2","It closes at five.")]
print("\n".join(f"[{i}] {t}" for i,t in passages))
examples.output:
[p1] The lab opens at nine.
[p2] It closes at five.

mistakes: A citation pointing to a retrieved passage does not establish that the passage supports the claim.
edges: Relevant passages may contradict each other or reflect different versions.
useCases: Grounded answer pipeline
Build an assistant that can answer questions about a local handbook.
practices: Store provenance and evaluate retrieval and answer generation separately.
rag.interview: Where can a RAG answer fail? Retrieval may miss evidence, context assembly may omit it or the model may misuse it.
rag.miniProject: Assemble a source-labeled prompt from a ranked passage list.
exercises: Assemble a source-labeled prompt from a ranked passage list.
Define an insufficient-evidence outcome for a question with no supported answer.

document-qa.definition: Document question answering finds and presents answers supported by a particular document collection.
document-qa.why: Let the reader open the exact handbook section underlying a response.
document-qa.explanation: Parse documents into chunks carrying stable source coordinates. Retrieve evidence for the question, preserve section context and show the evidence beside the answer.
document-qa.usage: Let the reader open the exact handbook section underlying a response.

examples.title: Check a quoted span
examples.code:
source = "The lab opens at 09:00 on weekdays."
print("09:00 on weekdays" in source)

mistakes: Chunking by character count alone can separate a condition from the rule it qualifies.
edges: Scanned PDFs may have no extractable text until an OCR step succeeds.
useCases: Document question-answering assistant
Let the reader open the exact handbook section underlying a response.
practices: Record source versions and report extraction failures.
document-qa.interview: How should the assistant handle an unreadable page? Flag the missing evidence and avoid unsupported answers.
document-qa.miniProject: Create chunks that retain a source name, page and section heading.
exercises: Create chunks that retain a source name, page and section heading.
Test a question whose answer crosses a paragraph boundary.

grounding.definition: Grounding connects generated claims to evidence the application can inspect. A hallucination is output that is unsupported or incorrect.
grounding.why: Reject an invented deadline even if the answer includes an existing citation ID.
grounding.explanation: Split an answer into checkable claims. Verify that each citation points to available evidence and that the evidence supports the wording, including qualifiers and dates.
grounding.usage: Reject an invented deadline even if the answer includes an existing citation ID.

examples.title: Detect a changed number in an extractive task
examples.code:
passage = "The deadline is 15 May."
print("16 May" in passage)

mistakes: Citation existence alone cannot show entailment.
edges: A correct claim may be absent from the permitted source set and should be marked unsupported for this task.
useCases: Evidence checker
Reject an invented deadline even if the answer includes an existing citation ID.
practices: Separate factual correctness from support by the supplied evidence.
grounding.interview: When is abstention appropriate? When the available evidence cannot answer the question with the required support.
grounding.miniProject: Annotate claims in an answer as supported, contradicted or missing evidence.
exercises: Annotate claims in an answer as supported, contradicted or missing evidence.
Rewrite an overconfident answer using the exact limits of the passage.

ai-evaluation.definition: AI evaluation measures how a system performs on a defined sample of realistic tasks.
ai-evaluation.why: Compare two assistant configurations on the same answerable and unanswerable questions.
ai-evaluation.explanation: Specify desired behavior and scoring rules before running a change. Record model and prompt versions. Analyze individual regressions alongside aggregate scores.
ai-evaluation.usage: Compare two assistant configurations on the same answerable and unanswerable questions.

examples.title: Find regressions

mistakes: An aggregate score can stay flat even as important individual cases regress.
edges: A small suite provides uncertain estimates, especially for rare failures.
useCases: Assistant evaluation scorecard
Compare two assistant configurations on the same answerable and unanswerable questions.
practices: Keep representative held-out cases and publish denominators with metrics.
ai-evaluation.interview: Why review examples behind a metric? They show which behaviors changed and whether the metric matches the goal.
ai-evaluation.miniProject: Define an evaluation set covering factual answers, abstention and malicious text.
exercises: Define an evaluation set covering factual answers, abstention and malicious text.
Compare two versioned runs and list newly failing questions.

ai-privacy.definition: AI privacy and security protect source documents, user inputs and privileged actions across model boundaries.
ai-privacy.why: Prevent one learner's private notes from appearing in another learner's answer.
ai-privacy.explanation: Treat retrieved documents and tool outputs as untrusted data. Filter access before retrieval, minimize what is sent to providers and enforce tool permissions outside the model.
ai-privacy.syntax:
docs = [{"id":1,"owner":"ada"},{"id":2,"owner":"lin"}]
print([d["id"] for d in docs if d["owner"]=="ada"])
ai-privacy.usage: Prevent one learner's private notes from appearing in another learner's answer.

examples.title: Filter by owner
examples.code:
docs = [{"id":1,"owner":"ada"},{"id":2,"owner":"lin"}]
print([d["id"] for d in docs if d["owner"]=="ada"])

mistakes: Placing secrets in a system prompt does not make them safe from exposure.
edges: Authorized sources can still contain malicious instructions targeting an agent.
useCases: Private document assistant
Prevent one learner's private notes from appearing in another learner's answer.
practices: Enforce authorization independently of generated text and record outbound data fields.
ai-privacy.interview: Why filter before retrieval? Inaccessible material should never enter contexts, logs or generated answers.
ai-privacy.miniProject: Trace every trust boundary in a document assistant and identify sent fields.
exercises: Trace every trust boundary in a document assistant and identify sent fields.
Test a document that tries to convince the assistant to disclose private notes.

linux.definition: Linux applications use files, processes, permissions and environment values to interact with their host.
linux.why: Diagnose a service that finds its files interactively but fails under a dedicated account.
linux.explanation: A process runs as a particular user with a working directory and environment. Relative paths depend on that working directory. Owner, group and other permission bits control basic file access.
linux.usage: Diagnose a service that finds its files interactively but fails under a dedicated account.

examples.title: Resolve a Unix-style path in memory

mistakes: Running a service as root to bypass a permissions error creates unnecessary privileges.
edges: Directory traversal requires execute permission on each directory in the path.
useCases: Service runbook
Diagnose a service that finds its files interactively but fails under a dedicated account.
practices: Record the service user, working directory and required writable paths.
linux.interview: Why can a relative path fail under a service manager? The service may start in a different working directory.
linux.miniProject: Write a runbook for inspecting a process and its configuration paths on Linux.
exercises: Write a runbook for inspecting a process and its configuration paths on Linux.
Explain the access granted by permissions 640 on a regular file.

docker.definition: A Docker image packages a filesystem and startup configuration. A container runs an instance of that image.
docker.why: Run a predictable API process while preserving learner data across container replacement.
docker.explanation: Build an image from a Dockerfile and versioned dependencies. Use a mounted volume or external store for durable data. Treat each running container as replaceable.
docker.usage: Run a predictable API process while preserving learner data across container replacement.
mistakes: Writing SQLite data only inside a container's writable layer can lose it when the container is removed.
edges: Binding to loopback inside a container can prevent the mapped host port from reaching the server.
useCases: Containerized API
Run a predictable API process while preserving learner data across container replacement.
practices: Pin dependencies and run the service as a minimally privileged user.
docker.interview: How does an image differ from a running container? One is a build artifact and the other is a process and writable runtime state.
docker.miniProject: Design a container specification for the employee API with an external data directory.
exercises: Design a container specification for the employee API with an external data directory.
List the checks needed before replacing the container with a new version.

ci-cd.definition: Continuous integration checks changes frequently. Continuous delivery prepares tested artifacts that can be deployed reliably.
ci-cd.why: Keep a broken learner assessment release from replacing a working service.
ci-cd.explanation: Build once, run checks and promote the same immutable artifact through environments. Make a failed test stop promotion and preserve enough metadata to identify a release.
ci-cd.usage: Keep a broken learner assessment release from replacing a working service.
mistakes: Rebuilding per environment can deploy a different artifact from the one you tested.
edges: A pipeline can pass with an empty test selection unless the runner checks the suite actually executed.
useCases: Release pipeline
Keep a broken learner assessment release from replacing a working service.
practices: Pin dependencies and record the artifact's immutable identity.
ci-cd.interview: What should happen after a failed integration test? Stop promotion and report the failing check with reproducible diagnostics.
ci-cd.miniProject: Draw a pipeline from commit through build, tests and staged deployment.
exercises: Draw a pipeline from commit through build, tests and staged deployment.
Specify how a failed migration prevents promotion.

cloud.definition: Cloud platforms provide managed compute, storage, networking and identity services.
cloud.why: Map a small API, its persistent data and its public entry point to cloud responsibilities.
cloud.explanation: Choose components by workload needs. A web process needs compute, durable data needs storage and access should flow through a scoped service identity. Separate application configuration from secrets.
cloud.usage: Map a small API, its persistent data and its public entry point to cloud responsibilities.
mistakes: Treating ephemeral compute disks as durable storage can lose data during replacement.
edges: Regional outages and cross-region traffic can affect recovery and cost.
useCases: Cloud deployment map
Map a small API, its persistent data and its public entry point to cloud responsibilities.
practices: Document the runtime identity, storage lifecycle and recovery assumptions.
cloud.interview: What is the benefit of a service identity? The workload can receive scoped access without embedding long-lived user credentials.
cloud.miniProject: Map the API to either AWS or Azure and name the component responsible for each resource.
exercises: Map the API to either AWS or Azure and name the component responsible for each resource.
Describe the data recovery procedure after compute replacement.

app-deployment.definition: Deployment moves a tested application version into an environment where users can reach it.
app-deployment.why: Verify that a new API version can read the expected database schema before it serves traffic.
app-deployment.explanation: Separate a process being alive from readiness to serve real requests. Release a version, check representative behavior and keep a tested recovery path if it fails.
app-deployment.usage: Verify that a new API version can read the expected database schema before it serves traffic.
mistakes: Marking a service ready before critical dependency checks pass can route users into failures.
edges: Rolling application code back may be unsafe after an incompatible database migration.
useCases: Release checklist
Verify that a new API version can read the expected database schema before it serves traffic.
practices: Plan migrations and rollback compatibility together.
app-deployment.interview: Why distinguish readiness from liveness? A process may be running while it cannot fulfill requests.
app-deployment.miniProject: Write a rollout checklist including a real user workflow and a rollback decision.
exercises: Write a rollout checklist including a real user workflow and a rollback decision.
Identify a schema migration that would break the previous application version.

secrets.definition: Secrets management controls how credentials are issued, injected, protected, rotated and revoked.
secrets.why: Connect an optional model provider without putting its key in Git history or logs.
secrets.explanation: Read a credential at runtime from an approved environment or secret store. Limit its scope, avoid exposing it to browser bundles and support rotation without changing application source.
secrets.usage: Connect an optional model provider without putting its key in Git history or logs.

examples.title: Redact an example field
examples.code:
sample = {"provider":"local","token":"example-only"}
print({k:"[redacted]" if k=="token" else v for k,v in sample.items()})

mistakes: Base64 encoding a credential leaves it recoverable by anyone who reads the value.
edges: Rotating a credential can leave old workers using a stale in-memory copy.
useCases: Provider credential plan
Connect an optional model provider without putting its key in Git history or logs.
practices: Expose a configured/unconfigured status instead of returning a secret value.
secrets.interview: Why revoke an accidentally committed key? Removing it from the latest file cannot remove prior copies.
secrets.miniProject: Write a rotation procedure that verifies the new credential and revokes the old one.
exercises: Write a rotation procedure that verifies the new credential and revokes the old one.
Test that configuration diagnostics omit the credential value.

production-logging.definition: Production logging collects structured events across running application instances for diagnosis.
production-logging.why: Follow a failing request through retrieval, model invocation and response validation.
production-logging.explanation: Use a stable schema with event name, release and request identifier. Limit retention and avoid high-volume payload dumps. Summarize repeated events while keeping a path back to a specific request.
production-logging.syntax:
from collections import Counter
events = ["success","timeout","timeout"]
print(Counter(events)["timeout"])
production-logging.usage: Follow a failing request through retrieval, model invocation and response validation.

examples.title: Group log events
examples.code:
from collections import Counter
events = ["success","timeout","timeout"]
print(Counter(events)["timeout"])

examples.title: Find a trace
examples.code:
records = [("r1","start"),("r2","start"),("r1","end")]
print([event for rid,event in records if rid=="r1"])

mistakes: Logging a raw prompt can expose internal documents even if the response is redacted.
edges: Retries can produce several records for one user operation.
useCases: Service event stream
Follow a failing request through retrieval, model invocation and response validation.
practices: Use request IDs and attempt numbers so repeated attempts remain interpretable.
production-logging.interview: What makes an event actionable? It identifies the operation, failure and enough safe context for diagnosis.
production-logging.miniProject: Define a shared event schema across three document assistant components.
exercises: Define a shared event schema across three document assistant components.
Summarize retries by operation without double-counting user requests.

monitoring.definition: Monitoring tracks behavior over time and signals when service quality crosses a meaningful boundary.
monitoring.why: Detect elevated error rates for answer requests while avoiding noise from isolated failures.
monitoring.explanation: Measure traffic, errors, latency and saturation. Choose a measurement window and denominator. Alert when sustained symptoms indicate a user impact that someone can act on.
monitoring.usage: Detect elevated error rates for answer requests while avoiding noise from isolated failures.

examples.title: Evaluate a sustained condition
examples.code:
windows = [0.03,0.04,0.05]
print(all(rate>0.02 for rate in windows))

mistakes: A global average latency can hide a long tail of very slow requests.
edges: Zero traffic makes a ratio's denominator zero and can itself signal a failure.
useCases: Service health dashboard
Detect elevated error rates for answer requests while avoiding noise from isolated failures.
practices: Pair an alert with an owner, a runbook and clear recovery behavior.
monitoring.interview: Why monitor user-visible outcomes? Healthy infrastructure can still serve incorrect or failing application responses.
monitoring.miniProject: Define three indicators for the assistant and a threshold with a time window.
exercises: Define three indicators for the assistant and a threshold with a time window.
Describe how the dashboard represents a period with no requests.

performance.definition: Performance engineering identifies bottlenecks and verifies improvements with measurements under representative load.
performance.why: Decide whether retrieval, generation or storage dominates response time.
performance.explanation: Split total latency into stages, measure distributions and optimize the dominant work. Check upper percentiles and resource use as concurrency increases. A cache changes both freshness and load.
performance.usage: Decide whether retrieval, generation or storage dominates response time.

examples.title: Compute a tiny nearest-rank p95
examples.code:
from math import ceil
times = sorted([12,15,18,90])
print(times[ceil(0.95*len(times))-1])

mistakes: Benchmarking only a warm cache can underrepresent first-request latency.
edges: A cache entry keyed only by query text can mix users with different access rights.
useCases: Latency investigation
Decide whether retrieval, generation or storage dominates response time.
practices: Measure before and after with the same workload and record correctness checks.
performance.interview: Why might mean latency improve while p95 worsens? A small fraction of increasingly slow requests can dominate the tail.
performance.miniProject: Measure stage times for a sample request and suggest a testable optimization.
exercises: Measure stage times for a sample request and suggest a testable optimization.
Design a permission-aware cache key and invalidation rule.

api-security.definition: API security controls access to operations and prevents abusive use of bounded resources.
api-security.why: Protect an expensive document-answer endpoint from unauthorized lookups and unbounded requests.
api-security.explanation: Authenticate callers, authorize each object and action, validate request size and limit expensive operations. A rate limit controls request frequency while per-request bounds control how much work one call can trigger.
api-security.usage: Protect an expensive document-answer endpoint from unauthorized lookups and unbounded requests.
mistakes: Rate limiting alone cannot stop one authorized request from asking for excessive work.
edges: Shared network addresses can group unrelated users under an IP-only limiter.
useCases: API abuse test plan
Protect an expensive document-answer endpoint from unauthorized lookups and unbounded requests.
practices: Test authorization using real object IDs owned by another test user.
api-security.interview: What makes insecure direct object references dangerous? Knowing an identifier must never substitute for an object-level permission check.
api-security.miniProject: Build a test plan for oversized requests, forbidden records and repeated calls.
exercises: Build a test plan for oversized requests, forbidden records and repeated calls.
Check that rejected requests cannot trigger provider costs.

testing.definition: Production-oriented testing verifies component interaction and critical behavior under realistic conditions and failures.
testing.why: Check that offline interview practice works when the question provider is unavailable.
testing.explanation: Combine fast deterministic checks with integration tests against disposable dependencies. A post-release smoke test runs a small representative workflow. Inject predictable failures to test recovery.
testing.syntax:
def choose(local, remote):
    return remote if remote is not None else local
assert choose(["curated"],None)==["curated"]
print("Fallback verified")
testing.usage: Check that offline interview practice works when the question provider is unavailable.

examples.title: Test a fallback rule
examples.code:
def choose(local, remote):
    return remote if remote is not None else local
assert choose(["curated"],None)==["curated"]
print("Fallback verified")

mistakes: A test that duplicates implementation logic can pass even when the shared assumption is wrong.
edges: A transient failure can happen after the server committed a change.
useCases: Release smoke suite
Check that offline interview practice works when the question provider is unavailable.
practices: Test observable outcomes with isolated fixtures and bounded waits.
testing.interview: Why inject a timeout? It verifies a recovery path that a healthy test dependency rarely exercises.
testing.miniProject: Define a smoke test from lesson to assessment to restored progress.
exercises: Define a smoke test from lesson to assessment to restored progress.
Inject a provider timeout and verify the local result remains usable.

cost.definition: Cost optimization reduces unnecessary resource use while preserving target quality and service levels.
cost.why: Estimate the cost of generated answers and detect retries that consume resources without improving outcomes.
cost.explanation: Identify the units charged by each dependency and measure them per successful user task. Compare cheaper configurations on the same evaluation set and enforce a bounded usage budget.
cost.usage: Estimate the cost of generated answers and detect retries that consume resources without improving outcomes.
mistakes: Treating illustrative rates as live provider prices gives unreliable forecasts.
edges: A cheaper model can increase total cost if it requires repeated attempts.
useCases: Request cost worksheet
Estimate the cost of generated answers and detect retries that consume resources without improving outcomes.
practices: Track cost alongside quality, latency and successful task count.
cost.interview: Why use cost per successful task? It includes the effect of failed attempts and gives spending an outcome denominator.
cost.miniProject: Compare two configurations using supplied unit rates and measured usage.
exercises: Compare two configurations using supplied unit rates and measured usage.
Set a maximum per-request budget that includes retry behavior.

agents.definition: An AI agent selects actions using observations, a goal and available tools.
agents.why: Build a research helper that can look up evidence and stop after a fixed number of attempts.
agents.explanation: A controller decides what actions are allowed and whether the loop should continue. Each step consumes time or budget. Define explicit success, failure and escalation conditions.
agents.syntax:
steps, limit, complete = 4, 4, False
print(steps < limit and not complete)
agents.usage: Build a research helper that can look up evidence and stop after a fixed number of attempts.

examples.title: Enforce a step cap
examples.code:
steps, limit, complete = 4, 4, False
print(steps < limit and not complete)

mistakes: Giving an agent unrestricted tools can turn a mistaken plan into a real external action.
edges: A tool can return a syntactically successful result containing no useful evidence.
useCases: Bounded research assistant
Build a research helper that can look up evidence and stop after a fixed number of attempts.
practices: Use a bounded action catalog, budget and verifiable termination rule.
agents.interview: What separates an agent from a single generation call? It can observe results and choose subsequent permitted actions.
agents.miniProject: Design a three-step research loop with a verified answer and a budget stop.
exercises: Design a three-step research loop with a verified answer and a budget stop.
Test the path in which every search returns no evidence.

tool-calling.definition: Tool calling lets a model propose a named operation and structured arguments for an application to evaluate.
tool-calling.why: Allow document lookup while rejecting unrecognized operations and inaccessible document IDs.
tool-calling.explanation: Validate the tool name, arguments and caller's permissions before dispatch. Return a bounded result that the model can interpret. Treat every proposed call as untrusted input.
tool-calling.usage: Allow document lookup while rejecting unrecognized operations and inaccessible document IDs.
mistakes: Using eval on generated tool names or arguments lets arbitrary code escape the intended interface.
edges: A schema-valid argument can reference a resource beyond the caller's permissions.
useCases: Validated lookup tool
Allow document lookup while rejecting unrecognized operations and inaccessible document IDs.
practices: Keep validation, authorization and execution in trusted application code.
tool-calling.interview: Who executes a proposed tool call? The application decides whether to dispatch and performs the operation.
tool-calling.miniProject: Implement an allowlist for two read-only tools with argument checks.
exercises: Implement an allowlist for two read-only tools with argument checks.
Reject a validly shaped request for a forbidden resource.

orchestration.definition: Orchestration coordinates steps, tools and state transitions across a task.
orchestration.why: Move a research task from retrieval to verification and then to an approved answer.
orchestration.explanation: Model the workflow as states with named transitions. Persist enough state to resume and make retries safe. A rejected transition should produce a traceable error rather than skip a required step.
orchestration.usage: Move a research task from retrieval to verification and then to an approved answer.
mistakes: Letting free-form output choose an arbitrary next state can bypass required validation.
edges: A crash between a tool side effect and recording the transition can duplicate work on resume.
useCases: Research workflow controller
Move a research task from retrieval to verification and then to an approved answer.
practices: Define idempotent steps or persist a deduplication key before external actions.
orchestration.interview: Why record transitions? They make failure recovery, auditing and regression analysis possible.
orchestration.miniProject: Design transitions for retrieve, verify, request clarification and finish.
exercises: Design transitions for retrieve, verify, request clarification and finish.
Simulate a crash during verification and describe a safe recovery.

memory-state.definition: State records what a workflow needs to continue. Memory stores information for potential use beyond the current interaction.
memory-state.why: Remember a learner's preferred study duration while keeping one assessment's partial answers private.
memory-state.explanation: Separate temporary task state from durable user facts. Store origin, scope and expiry for retained facts. Retrieve only information the current task is authorized to use.
memory-state.syntax:
record = {"user":"ada","key":"daily_minutes","value":120}
print(record["value"] if record["user"]=="ada" else None)
memory-state.usage: Remember a learner's preferred study duration while keeping one assessment's partial answers private.

examples.title: Scope a memory record
examples.code:
record = {"user":"ada","key":"daily_minutes","value":120}
print(record["value"] if record["user"]=="ada" else None)

examples.title: Expire an item using a fixed observation day

mistakes: Copying every conversation into durable memory can preserve errors and sensitive data unnecessarily.
edges: A once-correct preference can become stale or conflict with a newer user instruction.
useCases: Scoped learner memory
Remember a learner's preferred study duration while keeping one assessment's partial answers private.
practices: Keep provenance and support correction and deletion.
memory-state.interview: Why distinguish durable facts from working state? They have different lifetimes, access rules and trust requirements.
memory-state.miniProject: Design a scoped memory record with provenance, expiry and a deletion operation.
exercises: Design a scoped memory record with provenance, expiry and a deletion operation.
Resolve a stored preference that conflicts with a current explicit choice.

automation.definition: Automation executes a repeatable workflow in response to a trigger or schedule.
automation.why: Create one revision reminder per learner, topic and due date despite duplicate scheduling events.
automation.explanation: Treat triggers as potentially duplicated. Assign stable operation identities, record results and retry transient failures without repeating completed side effects. A compensating action may repair a step that cannot roll back.
automation.usage: Create one revision reminder per learner, topic and due date despite duplicate scheduling events.
mistakes: Checking for an existing record outside an atomic write permits two concurrent workers to create duplicates.
edges: A timeout after successful external delivery leaves an ambiguous outcome.
useCases: Revision reminder job
Create one revision reminder per learner, topic and due date despite duplicate scheduling events.
practices: Use a durable uniqueness constraint and an idempotent external interface where available.
automation.interview: Why does a retry need a stable key? The receiver can recognize an earlier successful execution of the same operation.
automation.miniProject: Design a reminder job with a unique identity and bounded retries.
exercises: Design a reminder job with a unique identity and bounded retries.
Describe recovery after a crash immediately following delivery.

multi-agent.definition: A multi-agent architecture divides work among agents with distinct responsibilities and coordination rules.
multi-agent.why: Separate evidence gathering from claim verification before publishing an answer.
multi-agent.explanation: Each role needs a bounded input, output and authority. Validate handoffs and attribute decisions to a role. Shared context consumes budget and can spread one agent's errors to others.
multi-agent.syntax:
packet = {"claim":"The lab opens at nine","evidence_id":"p2"}
print({"claim","evidence_id"} <= packet.keys())
multi-agent.usage: Separate evidence gathering from claim verification before publishing an answer.

examples.title: Validate a handoff
examples.code:
packet = {"claim":"The lab opens at nine","evidence_id":"p2"}
print({"claim","evidence_id"} <= packet.keys())

mistakes: Having several agents repeat the same unsupported assumption can look like independent agreement.
edges: A cycle of repeated handoffs can exhaust the budget without improving the result.
useCases: Research and review team
Separate evidence gathering from claim verification before publishing an answer.
practices: Compare against a simpler single-controller baseline and trace each handoff.
multi-agent.interview: What is the cost of splitting a task? Coordination, repeated context, delays and possible propagation of errors.
multi-agent.miniProject: Specify a researcher-to-reviewer packet and a deterministic stop rule.
exercises: Specify a researcher-to-reviewer packet and a deterministic stop rule.
Test a packet missing its evidence and record the rejection.

human-approval.definition: Human approval adds an explicit decision before a consequential action is executed.
human-approval.why: Require review before an assistant publishes or sends a generated report.
human-approval.explanation: Show the exact action, target and relevant parameters. Bind an approval to that reviewed payload, actor and lifetime. Revalidate both authorization and current state before execution.
human-approval.usage: Require review before an assistant publishes or sends a generated report.

examples.title: Bind approval to an exact proposal

agent-evaluation.why: Verify that a research assistant answers correctly, uses only allowed tools and stops on time.
agent-evaluation.explanation: Run tasks in an isolated environment with known fixtures. Check the final state, policy constraints, resource usage and tool sequence. A plausible answer can hide an unauthorized action.

llmops.definition: LLMOps manages the versions, evaluations, deployment and operational behavior of language-model applications.
llmops.why: Trace a decline in answer quality to the exact configuration change that introduced it.
llmops.explanation: A reproducible release identifies the model, prompt, retriever, data index and evaluation suite. Monitor latency, cost and quality. Keep the prior compatible configuration available for recovery.
llmops.usage: Trace a decline in answer quality to the exact configuration change that introduced it.

practices: Record available version identifiers, evaluation samples and release timestamps.

advanced-rag.definition: Advanced RAG combines retrieval and ranking strategies to improve evidence selection before answering.
advanced-rag.why: Retrieve both an exact policy code and a semantically related explanation.
advanced-rag.explanation: Lexical retrieval helps with exact terms while dense retrieval finds paraphrases. Fuse candidate sets, rerank a bounded shortlist and evaluate whether each component adds relevant evidence within latency limits.
advanced-rag.usage: Retrieve both an exact policy code and a semantically related explanation.
mistakes: Adding raw scores from unrelated retrieval systems assumes scales that may not be comparable.
edges: An effective reranker cannot recover evidence missing from its initial candidates.
useCases: Hybrid passage retriever

practices: Measure first-stage recall separately from reranked top-k quality.
advanced-rag.interview: What does an ablation test? Remove or replace one component while holding the rest fixed to estimate its contribution.

ai-architecture.definition: AI system architecture defines how ingestion, retrieval, inference, evaluation and user-facing services cooperate under constraints.
ai-architecture.why: Deliver a document assistant that continues offering local search when generation is unavailable.
ai-architecture.explanation: Start with user outcomes, trust boundaries and operation limits. Specify data contracts, retries and fallback behavior for every external dependency. Use measurable criteria for quality, latency, privacy and recovery.
